title: HomeFlood Limits, Deductible and Compliance Aid Statement Rule
content:
The following rule governs the limits and deductible written on HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies, both at issue and on any endorsement, and the private flood compliance aid statement.

**Limits.**
- The dwelling limit must lie between the tier's lowest and highest dwelling limit and may not exceed the dwelling replacement cost value.
- The dwelling replacement cost value must be at least the tier's lowest replacement cost value.
- The personal property limit must lie between the tier's lowest and highest personal property limit.
- Limits are written in whole multiples of the tier's limit increment.

**Deductible.** The deductible is one per-occurrence amount from the tier's list of deductible options, not below the tier's lowest deductible. When the application elects none, the tier's default deductible applies.

**Compliance aid statement.** The policy carries the private flood compliance aid statement only when both of these hold:
- the tier's form is at least as broad as the SFIP (the tier can carry the statement);
- the elected deductible is no more than the tier's highest compliance-aid deductible.

The statement is decided again on every endorsement that changes the deductible.

**Mortgage-required policies.** A mortgage-required policy is written only when it carries the compliance aid statement, because only then must the lender accept it in place of NFIP coverage. A request that would leave a mortgage-required policy without the statement is not processed. Both the mortgage requirement and the statement are judged on the policy the request concerns.

| Tier can carry the statement | Deductible at or below the highest compliance-aid deductible | Statement | Mortgage-required issue or endorsement |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | carried | processed |
| yes | no | not carried | not processed |
| no | yes | not carried | not processed |
| no | no | not carried | not processed |

*Hypothetical illustration:* a mortgage-required HomeFlood Premier policy asks to raise its deductible to a figure above the highest compliance-aid deductible. The request would leave the policy without the statement, so it is not processed.

The tier figures the rule reads (the tier's ability to carry the statement, its highest dwelling limit and its lowest deductible) are those of the tier's own schedules.
